items.title: Normalization and abelian normal-module bound
items.assessment: The minimal quotient subfamily remains irredundant in the quotient. Each corrected extra element is independent relative to the generated base by direct substitution. For an abelian normal kernel, G=N*base makes its full conjugation action equal to the base action. This proves maximum irredundant-length bounds; it never substitutes minimum generator number. Cameron–Cara Theorem1.1 is explicitly attributed and proved in full.

items.title: Degree-nine signed cyclic modules
items.assessment: A block 3-cycle acts on F3^3 with minimal polynomial (X-delta)^3 and one Jordan block; invariant submodules form a chain and a member of maximal valuation-span contains the others. On F2^3 the cyclic action has one trivial and one irreducible two-dimensional summand. Normal-module costs one and two, with quotient at most two, give five.

items.title: Module quotients and blocks of size two, three and four
items.assessment: For an irredundant module family, maximal submodules omitting one member give a surjection onto the direct sum of simple quotients. The coordinate-axis image argument is valid even with isomorphic simple factors. Transitive binary fixed vectors and functionals each have dimension one. The full symmetric group bound two follows from transposition differences. Ternary full-block-image cost m would force abelian action, contradicting its S_m permutation image. For S4 blocks, the odd-order normal subgroup projects onto each C3, has no fixed vector, and averaging makes fixed points exact on subquotients, forcing simple quotients to have dimension at least two. The m=3 block-three case is separately covered.

items.title: All-degree primitive bounds
items.assessment: Read original Maroti Theorem1.1 including A_m^ell lower containment, not the weakened reprint. Product-action groups act faithfully on m*ell letters; nonnatural subset actions satisfy m<=n/2. The residual order envelope is verified for26..63 and proved from64 onward. The complete primitive catalogue deals with9..25. The twelve exceptional groups use exact maximal-subgroup/socle/quotient facts and Whiston. In particular M11 parabolics lie in involution-generated subgroups; M12 maximal groups are handled separately. No equality with string C-rank or recovery of the printed exact census is inferred.

items.title: Subdirect chains and normalized simple kernels
items.assessment: The elementary Scott argument inducts on coordinates, separating trivial/full last-coordinate kernel and using commuting normal images of diagonal simple factors. Increasing subdirect chains refine the partition, giving at most m-1 steps. The simple-kernel proof first chooses the quotient generators, then a minimal subset of normalized extras whose conjugate projection generates one factor. Choosing one witness from each indispensable projected subgroup gives an independent family in S. The quotient generators already act transitively on coordinates because N fixes them. All remaining additions strictly enlarge the kernel intersection. This proves the stated uniform maximum-length inequality.

items.title: Primitive block action and all small exceptions
items.assessment: Read all eleven finite exceptions and their subgroup rather than merely whole-group bounds. AGL3(2) splits by translation intersection dimension and irreducibility; line/plane stabilizers are S4. Frattini reduction handles GL2(3); remaining normal and maximal group inputs are checked by the required program. The unique degree-six S5 exception is retained explicitly.

items.title: Universal imprimitive bound, all n>=9
items.assessment: A minimal nontrivial block has primitive setwise-stabilizer action. Cases k=2,3,4 use the preceding module arguments with all small (k,m) ranges covered. For k>=5, proper block images give the coordinate bounds; two-block primitive images use the stronger independent-family lemma. The alternating/symmetric cases have kernel projection1/A_k/S_k and subdirect alternating intersection. The simple-kernel bound and binary quotient cover m>=3 and m=2 separately. The exceptional degree-six S5 two-block case has bound6<=8. No sample transitive group or finite maximum-generator search substitutes for this proof. The alternating parabolic exclusion uses IP, normality and the trivial centralizer of A_n.

items.title: All-subset attachment formula
items.assessment: Checked all four finite hypotheses for every S,R, including mixed Young intersections and partition meets. The subgroup formula is proved for an arbitrary subset of tree edges by saturation at the root and transposition conjugation. Intersections split into both-root-singleton, exactly-one, and neither-singleton cases. In the latter case the leaf condition ensures a shared first edge; without it the conclusion is false. The independent V4/two-leaf model gives intersection S4 rather than V4. No maximal-parabolic shortcut is used.

items.title: Exact tree presentations and transport
items.assessment: The triangle-ordering braid equivalences are valid. Induction identifies the old subgroup with S_(n-1), proves the new leaf generator centralizes the old root stabilizer, and closes a union of at most n cosets under generators. This is an upper-bound proof, not merely a permutation quotient. The transport lemma includes both the substituted old relators and all forward marking identities, so its homomorphisms are inverse. Independent path/star/two-branch S6 presentations pass; a finite affine A2 quotient refutes omitting triangle relations. The text calls H*a*f_v left cosets although they are right cosets under the usual terminology; the explicit multiplication proof fixes the convention and is correct.

items.title: Rank n-1 in all degrees n>=7
items.assessment: Whiston W1 and the exact W2 omission alternatives are expressly retained through Cameron–Cara. The imprimitive exclusion also covers the needed m=4 boundary by the binary module calculation. The alternating omission is excluded with IP. One orbit-crossing edge per mark gives a tree; an additional edge would make a forbidden bypass. Conversely forest intersections prove IP, laminar subsets prove flag completion, and the shared coset argument gives all geometry claims.

items.title: The three complete finite cores
items.assessment: The accepted source diagrams were visually matched to the explicit A/B D8 markings and C V4 marking. Their chosen roots distinguish the two D8 centralizer orbits and the single V4 orbit. Every finite attachment hypothesis has a written group/partition proof, including empty/singleton/full supports and saturation by a new transposition; the156 tests are validation. The tail root is explicitly a leaf, but branching after the first edge is allowed.

items.title: Exhaustive fracture graph alternatives
items.assessment: The selected n-2 edges give a forest with two components. The bypass argument restricts any cycle to its extra-edge labels. Two disjoint extra edges contradict matching/path lengths; two intersecting distinct-endpoint edges force an alternating square and exclude a third. Otherwise all extras are parallel, each repeated label is a double transposition with the same extra factor. These structural arguments exhaust arbitrary degree, not a finite marking list.

items.title: Every local continuation and the five-letter boundaries
items.assessment: Checked cube splitting of a double transposition meeting a new edge, and generation of S5 by the two path factors plus connector. The path/star five-letter cases allow precisely five untwisted and three twisted extensions each; all eight are excluded by explicit common transposition and common-label subgroup arguments. A repeated mark cannot meet the existing common factor, which justifies the restricted twist list. The18 finite witness rows actually give the stated common transpositions, with the last two in their own relabelled coordinates.

items.title: Long separation and parallel repetitions
items.assessment: If separation exceeds one, first/last connectors give a common transposition with too small common support; repeated end connectors are split into at least-three and exactly-two intermediate-edge cases. The exactly-two case invokes the exhaustive five-letter extension lemma using connectedness and n>5. Two distinct repeated marks either have distinct connectors and a common transposition on disjoint supports, or share a connector and give the star boundary. No unexamined third case remains.

items.title: Exactly A, B and C
items.assessment: The remaining core is D8 or V4. Two outgoing edges yield two full symmetric extensions with intersection Sym(Q), strictly larger than the core, contradicting IP. Thus there is a single attached tree. The centralizer orbits give exactly the two D8 root choices or the unique V4 choice. Sufficiency then invokes the fully checked attachment theorem and the separate flag proof.

items.title: All decorated flags and full automorphism group
items.assessment: Read exact stabilizers for ordinary subsets, bridge four-sets with matching decoration, and both core types. Pair-incidence rules yield a simultaneous bijection on at most three core points. If the bridge is present, each of A/B/C has an explicit compatible matching completion. Weighted laminar regions, with root weight four, allow independent bijections extending it to every chosen tail subset. This proves all flags have a common representative; IP alone is not substituted for flag transitivity. Thin panels, residual connectedness and chamber connectivity then make the full type-preserving automorphism group exactly S_n.

items.title: Every branch and source correction
items.assessment: Checked both forward and inverse marking words, all local pair orders, arbitrary tail incidence, and every local Cor6.5(5) word. The common transport theorem supplies an exact general presentation including all inverse-word consistency relations. Literal Cor6.5(2) fails in the exhibited S9 marking with two order-three tail neighbours of the uniquely order-six-identified bridge. The accepted source p17 image confirms the false commutation clause; no blanket equivalence with the shorter printed presentation is asserted.

items.title: Auxiliary example and deliberate exclusions
items.assessment: The six literal source involutions are matched on physicalp15. The program proves S8, all4096 IP intersections, all156 complete product-set conditions, and the actual transitive parabolic order1344. The all-anchor flag criterion is proved by induction. The exact Table1 C-rank census, the unfixed leaves-versus-leaf-orbits count, and unused general background theorems remain explicit exclusions. They are not silently called recovered, while all five declared principal targets are handled in their full ranges or explicitly corrected form.
